sections.content:
Interesting! Clicking the top-left tile caused a big animation (17 frames, 65 cells changed). All 9 tiles in the grid are now gray (g). This is very different from what I expected.
Looking at the animation objects, it affected all 5 cross-pattern tiles plus the top-left handle area. The top bar also changed - the blue handle moved to the right side of the gray bar.
This suggests that clicking a tile when ALL cross-pattern tiles are green triggers some kind of "submit" or "check" action, which then resets all tiles to gray. The handle on the top bar moved, suggesting progress was made (or a check was performed).
Let me reconsider the mechanics:
1. Click tiles to turn them green (N)
2. When all 4 cross-pattern tiles are green, clicking one of them submits/checks the pattern
3. If correct, the handle moves and tiles reset
4. Maybe I need to do this multiple times? Or maybe the handle position matters?
Looking at the top bar, the blue handle moved from the left side to the right side. This could mean:
- The pattern was correct and the handle advanced
- Or the pattern was wrong and the handle moved to indicate failure
Let me look at the purple dot pattern again. The purple dots form a cross: top-center, middle-left, middle-right, bottom-center. I made those 4 tiles green, plus accidentally made top-left green too. When I clicked top-left, everything reset.
Wait - maybe the issue is that I had 5 green tiles instead of 4. The extra top-left tile made the pattern wrong, so it reset. Let me try again, making ONLY the 4 cross-pattern tiles green, and then clicking one of them to submit.
Actually, looking more carefully at the animation: it affected tiles at positions (49,29), (54,24), (54,34), (59,29) - these are the 4 cross-pattern positions. And (49,24) which is top-left. So all 5 green tiles were affected.
Let me try again: make exactly the 4 cross-pattern tiles green, then click one to submit. But this time I need to be careful not to click top-left.
